description: OpenMC is a Monte Carlo particle transport code that aims to be fully featured and based on modern methods. It is a constructive solid geometry, continuous-energy transport code that uses cross sections in HDF5 format, and it began in the Computational Reactor Physics Group at MIT; the licence names MIT, UChicago Argonne LLC and the OpenMC contributors as copyright holders. The reference publication is Romano and co-authors, Annals of Nuclear Energy 82 (2015). Documentation for the stable and development versions is on Read the Docs, and support is through a discussion forum. The code is free under the MIT licence on GitHub, with releases up to v0.16.0 among the tags read, Python 3.12 or later required by the package metadata, and commits up to 19 September 2026. Coverage is general geometries and materials. Caveats: results depend on the cross section data used and on statistical convergence, and runs can be computationally heavy. Simulation uses are reactor physics and shielding calculations that feed safety and fuel cycle analyses of nuclear plants. Related records: model-cardinal couples OpenMC with NekRS inside MOOSE, and platform-moose-multiphysics-framework is the host framework.
